title: Begin in His name, and the whole thing changes.
subtitle: The opening words of the Opener
then: Al-Fatihah was among the very first complete surahs revealed in Makkah. It is called the Mother of the Book, the Opener, and the seven oft-repeated verses. {idea}The first thing it says about Allah is mercy, said twice.{/idea}
now: You open the laptop for a hard email. You start the car for a long drive. You pick up the phone to call your mother after an argument. Most of us start things in our own name, on our own strength. {reward}This verse offers a different starting point.{/reward}
old: I start things on my own and hope they work out.
new: When I begin in His name, I begin already surrounded by mercy.
try: Before the next task you dread today, pause and say Bismillah slowly, meaning it.

title: All praise already belongs to Him.
subtitle: Praise as the first word of the prayer
then: The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah divides this prayer between Himself and His servant. {idea}When the servant says all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, Allah says: My servant has praised Me.{/idea} The prayer is a two-way conversation.
now: You recite it five times a day, often while thinking about dinner or a deadline. Picture instead that every line gets an answer. {reward}You are not reading to a wall.{/reward} Someone is replying to you, by name, as you speak.
old: Al-Fatihah is something I say quickly to get the prayer going.
new: Each line I say is heard and answered by the Lord of the worlds.
try: In your next prayer, pause one breath after this verse, as if waiting for the reply.

title: The Lord of everything leads with mercy.
subtitle: Why mercy comes right after lordship

picture.label: What follows Lord of the worlds

then: Straight after naming Allah as Lord of all the worlds, the servant names His mercy again. In the same hadith of the divided prayer, {idea}Allah answers this line: My servant has glorified Me.{/idea}
now: Think of the most powerful person you know: a manager, a landlord, a judge. Power usually makes people nervous. {reward}Here the One with all power introduces Himself by mercy, twice.{/reward} That is who you are speaking to when you stand to pray.
old: Someone that powerful must be waiting to punish me.
new: The One who owns everything chose to be known first by His mercy.
try: Remember one mercy you received this week that you did nothing to earn. Thank Him for it.

title: One Day belongs to Him alone.
subtitle: Mercy now, and a Day when all is settled
then: After praise and mercy comes the Day of Recompense. In the hadith of the divided prayer, Allah answers this line: {idea}My servant has related all matters to Me.{/idea} The servant hands over the final word.
now: A coworker takes credit for your work. A relative cheats you out of an inheritance and gets away with it. {trap}It feels like the story ends there.{/trap} This verse says it does not. {idea}There is a Day that belongs to Allah alone, and nothing is lost on it.{/idea}
old: If no one sees it now, it is gone forever.
new: Every account is kept and settled on a Day only Allah owns.
try: Think of one wrong done to you that still stings. Hand it to Allah in a short dua.

title: You alone we serve, You alone we ask.
subtitle: The middle line, shared between Allah and you
then: This is the turning point of the surah. In the hadith of the divided prayer, Allah says of this verse: {idea}This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asked for.{/idea} Worship and asking for help are joined.
now: You pray, then spend the night scrolling job sites in a panic, as if everything rests on you. Or you ask everyone for help except Him. {trap}Worship goes one way, reliance another.{/trap} This verse ties them together in one breath.
old: I pray to Allah, but in practice I lean on my own plans.
new: The One I worship is the One I lean on, and He promised to answer.
try: Before you ask anyone for help with something today, ask Allah for it first, in your own words.

title: The one thing to ask for: show me the way.
subtitle: A prayer the rest of the Quran answers
then: Al-Fatihah was placed first as a prayer for anyone who opens the Quran. {idea}The servant asks to be guided, and the Master answers by placing the whole Quran before him.{/idea} Allah says of this part: This is for My servant.
now: Your dua list is long: the job, the visa, the test result, the marriage. Then this line, asked many times a day, quietly asks for the thing under all of them. {reward}A direction you can trust, whatever happens to the list.{/reward}
old: Guidance is something I already have; I need other things.
new: Even on my best day, I still need to be shown the way.
try: Open the Quran today and read one page as the answer to this exact request.

title: Walk where the favored walked, not where others slipped.
subtitle: A path with people already on it
then: The prayer ends by naming the path through people: those Allah favored, set against two ways to lose it. {idea}Allah says of these last lines: This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asked for.{/idea}
now: You do not have to invent a good life from scratch. Someone before you was patient through illness, honest at work, kind to a hard parent. {reward}The path has footprints.{/reward} {trap}And you can also see where people drifted off it, and learn.{/trap}
old: I have to work out what a good life looks like by myself.
new: The straight path is a road others already walked, and I can follow them.
try: Think of one person whose faith you admire. Copy one small habit of theirs today.
